policy: Every number carries a status. 'reported' = taken from the project's own write-ups and not re-run here (it needs private data). 'measured' = produced by a command in this repository. 'not_measured' / 'unvalidated' = known gaps, listed on purpose.

cv5_stage2.title: 5-fold cross-validation of Stage 2, out-of-fold
cv5_stage2.protocol: Images are grouped by similarity (threshold 0.85) so that near-duplicates never straddle folds. Each fold trains on the other four and is measured on images its model never saw; best-epoch selection uses the fold's own validation part, not the measured part. Stage-2 crops are cut around the label with a uniform random offset of up to 35 px in x and y, simulating Stage-1 localisation error.

holdout50.title: Single held-out test split
holdout50.protocol: 337 cleaned images split 236 / 51 / 50 (train / val / test) by similarity group. The test split is used once for reporting.
holdout50.model: Two-stage pipeline, PyTorch (earlier 2-landmark generation; the source does not state the model generation of the decision table separately)

notes: Errors are in pixels of the 640 x 640 stretched training images.

The label noise floor for axillary points is the measured disagreement between independent labels of the same photo; for spine points (5.58) it is a leave-one-out upper bound estimated without relabelling.
Natural spread between folds is 2.1 px: differences smaller than that between two configurations are not statistically meaningful.
Signal is the median absolute value of the quantity across the dataset, i.e. the size of what is being measured. Error / signal is derived from the two columns.
The single-label noise floor is 0.435 degrees; averaging independent labels lowered it to 0.232 (233 of 337 images carry averaged labels).
These are Stage-2 errors with simulated coarse seeds, NOT an end-to-end measurement with real Stage-1 outputs and NOT an on-device measurement.

Provenance correction: the previous README attributed this table to the 5-fold cross-validation. The same figures appear in MOBIL_YAPILACAKLAR.md under the n = 50 test split, and '15 of 16 positives' cannot come from a 337-image evaluation, so they are filed here as held-out n = 50 results. Re-run scripts/20 to confirm.
Wilson 95 % intervals are computed from the counts at render time. With 4 to 16 positives they are wide: the 7 degree row (4 of 4) cannot support any claim.
Thresholds apply to the axillary tilt, which is a surface-asymmetry indicator, not a Cobb angle.
Stage 1 alone gave the same ~24 px error on train, validation and test, i.e. it could not even fit its own training data: the bottleneck is the representation, not the amount of data.
10 % of points still deviate by more than 10 px; the tail is mostly bent or atypical poses.

All 42 JVM tests were run on 2026-10-31 with Gradle 8.10.2 and JDK 17: 42 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The 42 includes PerformansTest, a timing test with a very loose bound, and a test of the uncalibrated Cobb placeholder (see gaps).

rows.item: Duplicate clusters with left/right label conflicts
Left/right accuracy of a COCO pose model on back views

notes: Source: a Roboflow export (see docs/DATA_AND_LICENSING.md). The images are web-sourced and resized to 640 x 640 without preserving aspect ratio; the originals are unavailable.

rows.approach: Spine trace by image processing (shadow valley)
rows.result: Residual RMS 9.20 % of torso height; 2 of 110 images gave a usable trace.
rows.reason: The lowest-intensity point is usually a scapula edge or side shadow, not the spinal groove.

rows.approach: Polynomial fit to average out landmark noise
rows.reason: Landmark errors are correlated, so the curve moves with the error.

rows.result: Convexity-direction accuracy fell from 0.639 to 0.550 (chance baseline 0.494).
Silhouette-width profile agreed with the colour cue 50 % of the time (chance).
rows.reason: Skin-tone centroid gives no signal on greyscale images.

rows.result: Lateral error 5.88 px vs label floor 5.58 px vs signal 6.50 px; convexity accuracy 63.9 % vs 52.8 % for always guessing the majority class.
rows.reason: The limit is label quality, not the model.

rows.result: About 24 px error on train, validation and test alike.

gaps.what: Latency of Stage 1 + 7 x Stage 2 on a phone, and RAM, energy and thermal behaviour.
gaps.why: Only shutter latency was ever measured on the device. scripts/31 prints a ~100-200 ms target but that was written when the pipeline refined 2 points, not 7.
gaps.next: Run the benchmark protocol in docs/BENCHMARKING.md on at least one low-end and one mid-range phone.

gaps.what: Accuracy of the full chain with real Stage-1 outputs for all 7 landmarks.
gaps.why: The cross-validation seeds Stage 2 with simulated (+-35 px) offsets instead of real Stage-1 predictions.
gaps.next: Out-of-fold Stage 1 as well, then evaluate the chain on the out-of-fold images.

gaps.what: Quantisation cost of the 7-landmark TFLite models.
gaps.why: Measured only for the 2-landmark models (about +0.04 degrees).

gaps.what: Accuracy on photographs captured with a phone under the intended protocol.
gaps.why: Training and evaluation images are web-sourced; the phone data amounts to a handful of informal captures.
gaps.next: Collect 200-300 protocol-conformant phone photos with a second independent labelling round.

gaps.what: The Cobb-angle estimate and risk category shown on the Android overlay (Kalibrasyon.cobbTahmini, scripts/48_cobb_kalibrasyon.py).
gaps.why: Its coefficients (1.25 / 1.10 / 2.40) and the '+-3.5 degree' error margin are not fitted to any radiograph-matched data - none exists in this project - and contradict the project's own rule that the interface must not state a Cobb angle. Treat it as a placeholder, not a measurement.
gaps.next: Remove it from the UI, or gate it behind a debug flag, until it is calibrated on radiograph-paired data.
